newsitem.title: USA: Dow posts solid gain, powered by strong earnings.
newsitem.headline: Dow posts solid gain, powered by strong earnings.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks staged their strongest rally in three weeks on Monday, propelled by better-than-expected earnings reports from several companies.
The Dow industrials rose 60 points to close unofficially at 6452. The advance was the Dow's largest in point terms since a 100.46 point surge on March 24.

Analysts said nervous investors found some relief when a series of leading multinationals, including Coca-Cola Co and General Motors Corp, announced first-quarter profits that exceeded Wall Street's estimates.
"Today's rally suggests select stocks with good earnings may put some bounce back in the market," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
To be sure, several analysts cautioned that market sentiment was still guarded, particularly with the Consumer Price Index (CPI), a key measure of inflation, due on Tuesday.

"In general, results are coming in better than expected, but we've still got a test tomorrow in the CPI," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates. "Today certainly doesn't mean we're out of the woods."
The looming CPI report held the bond market in check, where yields on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury edged up one basis point to 7.17 percent.

The quiet bond market left equity investors free to focus on the generally favorable earnings news. In addition to Coca-Cola, which rallied two points to 55-3/4, and GM, which gained 1/2 to 53-1/2, Travelers Inc also produced a favorable profit surprise and climbed two points to 48-3/8.
Analysts said the results provided a much-needed psychological boost for investors, who had watched the Dow dive nearly 10 percent during the last five weeks.
"This market has been groping for a near-term bottom," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "It looks like we may have found one."
"But there are definitely people still sitting this out," he said. "I expect this market to remain extremely choppy."

Investors got more favorable news after the close when Intel Corp reported first-quarter earnings of $2.20 per share, beating analysts' estimates and hitting a so-called "whisper number" that had been circulating around Wall Street.
Intel jumped to 135 in after-hours trading after a regular session that lifted the shares 3-1/4 to 133-1/4.
"Intel's number is an important one for the psychology of the market," Ackerman said, adding that the company was one of a handful that set the tone for technology shares.
Tech stocks generally turned in a solid performance, pacing the Nasdaq Composite to a 9.51 point gain to 1216.41.

One notable exception was Novellus Systems Inc, which tumbled 22-1/4 to 53 after the company announced it had lost a patent infringement trial. Novellus also said its first-quarter earnings fell sharply from the same period a year earlier.
Among other individual issues, Shaw Group Inc slid 8-5/8 to 13 after warning of weak earnings in the third and fourth quarters of its fiscal year.
Container carrier APL Ltd jumped 8-1/4 to 29-3/4 after agreeing to be acquired by Singaporean shipping company Neptune Orient Lines Ltd in a deal worth $825 million, or $33.50 per APL share.
The S&P 500 index rose 6.08 points to 743.73.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
